issues.t: Internal water pump leaks coolant into the oil
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping with no puddle under the car, a sweet smell, milky or tan-colored oil, overheating, or low oil pressure. Left alone it can end in engine knocking and total engine failure.
issues.why: The water pump on the 3.5L V6 sits inside the engine behind the timing cover and is turned by the timing chain. When its seal wears out, coolant can drain straight into the oil pan instead of dripping outside, where it thins the oil and wipes out the bearings.
issues.next: Watch the coolant level. If it drops for no visible reason or the oil looks milky, stop driving and have a shop pressure-test the cooling system and check the oil. Catching it early means a water pump job; catching it late often means a replacement engine.

issues.t: Engine failure after coolant contamination or oil starvation
issues.sym: Knocking from the bottom of the engine, oil pressure light, loss of power, or the engine seizing, often with little warning.
issues.why: Owners most often report complete engine failure on the 2009-2010 Flex. Many cases trace back to the internal water pump letting coolant into the oil, which destroys the crankshaft bearings.
issues.next: Never ignore an oil pressure light or knocking. Pull over and shut the engine off. Ask the shop to check the oil for coolant so you know the root cause before paying for a replacement engine.

issues.t: AWD power transfer unit (PTU) leaks or fails
issues.sym: Gear oil leaking near the passenger side of the engine, a burnt-oil smell, grinding or whining from under the front of the car, or the AWD not working.
issues.why: The power transfer unit sends power to the rear wheels on AWD models. It holds a small amount of oil, runs hot next to the exhaust, and its seals wear out. Once the oil leaks out or cooks, the gears wear quickly.
issues.next: If you smell hot gear oil or see a leak, have the PTU checked and its fluid changed. Fixing seals early can prevent replacing the whole unit.

issues.t: Wheel bearing hum or growl
issues.sym: A humming, growling or roaring noise that rises with speed, often above 40 mph, and may change when you turn. In bad cases the ABS light comes on.
issues.why: Wheel bearings and hubs are the most-reported repair on the Flex in TrueDelta's owner survey. The hubs can also rust to the steering knuckle, which makes the job harder.
issues.next: Have the noisy corner identified on a lift. Replace the bearing before it gets loose, because a badly worn bearing affects steering and the ABS.

issues.t: Door ajar light stays on
issues.sym: The door ajar warning stays on with all doors shut, the interior lights stay on or flicker, and the battery may go dead overnight.
issues.why: A switch inside one of the door latches wears or corrodes and keeps telling the car the door is open.
issues.next: Find which door the dash says is open. Spraying the latch with lubricant can help for a while, but the lasting fix is a new door latch.

issues.t: Rear side window shatters on its own
issues.sym: A loud bang and a rear side or quarter window suddenly breaking into small pieces, sometimes while parked or driving on a smooth road.
issues.why: Owners report the tempered rear side glass breaking without being hit. Stress in the glass or its mounting is suspected, but Ford has not issued a recall for it.
issues.next: Cover the opening to keep water out and have the glass replaced. Note the date and conditions and file a complaint with NHTSA, which helps track the problem.

issues.t: Roof drain tubes clog and leak water inside
issues.sym: Water dripping from the headliner, wet carpet or seats, a musty smell, or water stains around the roof glass or A-pillars after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: Cars with the Vista Roof glass have drain tubes that carry water down the pillars. The tubes can clog, kink or come loose, and some were reported to be poorly connected from the factory.
issues.next: Have the drain tubes cleared and checked for connection. Dry the interior quickly to avoid mold and electrical problems.

issues.t: Clicking behind the dash from the blend door actuator
issues.sym: A repeated clicking or tapping from behind the dashboard, often after starting the car, or one side of the cabin blowing hot while the other blows cold.
issues.why: The small electric motors that move the air doors in the heater box have plastic gears that strip, and their position sensors wear out.
issues.next: It is not a safety issue. Have the noisy actuator identified and replaced when the noise or temperature split bothers you.

issues.t: Front airbag may not fully inflate (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign in most cases. You may get a recall letter from Ford.
issues.why: On a small number of Flexes, the second stage of a front airbag may not inflate correctly in a crash, which raises injury risk. NHTSA recall 16V-247.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the airbag replaced free at a Ford dealer.

issues.t: Power steering assist can suddenly cut out (recall)
issues.sym: Steering suddenly becomes very heavy, especially at low speeds, and a power steering warning may appear.
issues.why: A fault in the electric power steering system can shut off assist. The recall (15V-340) covers 2011-2012 Flexes with the EcoBoost and all 2013 models.
issues.next: Hold the wheel firmly and drive slowly to a safe place; you can still steer, it just takes more effort. Have the recall done; a dealer updates the steering software or replaces the steering gear.

issues.t: Fuel delivery module can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell, fuel dripping under the car, or a fuel stain near the rear of the car.
issues.why: The plastic fuel delivery module on top of the fuel tank can crack and leak fuel, which could start a fire. NHTSA recalls 13V-227 and 15V-812.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, park outdoors away from buildings and call a Ford dealer. The fix is free.

issues.t: Halfshaft can disengage and lose drive (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power to the wheels, a clunk, or the car rolling while in Park if the parking brake is not set.
issues.why: On some 2013-2014 models the halfshaft or linkshaft can separate from the transmission or PTU, cutting drive. NHTSA recall 14V-393.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake when parking until the recall is done. Have a Ford dealer inspect and repair it for free.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may switch off wrongly (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag OFF light stays on with an adult in the seat.
issues.why: The passenger seat's occupant sensing system could classify an adult as a child or empty seat and turn the airbag off. NHTSA recall 14V-710.
issues.next: Have the free recall repair done. Until then, keep adults in mind when the OFF light is lit with them seated.

issues.t: Fuel pump can lose power and stall (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving or will not restart, sometimes with no warning.
issues.why: The fuel pump driver module could lose power, which shuts off the fuel pump. NHTSA recall 16V-621.
issues.next: If it stalls, steer to safety with the hazard lights on. Check your VIN for open recalls; a Ford dealer will fix it under the recall.

issues.t: Parking brake may not hold (recall)
issues.sym: The car can roll even with the parking brake set.
issues.why: A problem in the parking brake on some 2015 models could keep it from holding fully. NHTSA recall 15V-464.
issues.next: Always shift into Park and park on level ground until the recall is done. A dealer repairs it free.

issues.t: Turbo oil line can leak and cause a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Oil smell, smoke from under the hood, or oil spots under the engine.
issues.why: A turbocharger oil supply line on some EcoBoost engines could leak oil onto hot exhaust parts, which could start a fire. NHTSA recall 16V-925.
issues.next: If you see smoke, pull over and shut off the engine. Check your VIN; the replacement line is free at a Ford dealer.

issues.t: Rear toe link can break (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from the rear, the car pulling or wandering, or a sudden change in handling.
issues.why: The rear suspension toe link can fracture, which can make the car hard to control. NHTSA recall 20V-072 covers over 200,000 Flexes and related models.
issues.next: Get the recall done right away. If you feel the rear end suddenly wander, slow down and have the car towed.

issues.t: Loose alternator or starter cables (recall)
issues.sym: Dim lights, battery warning, the engine not cranking, or a burning smell from under the hood.
issues.why: Battery cables at the alternator or starter may not have been tightened properly at the factory, which can cause stalling, no-start or a fire. NHTSA recall 18V-548.
issues.next: Do not ignore a burning smell. Check your VIN; a dealer will tighten or repair the cables free.

issues.t: Rearview camera may show a blank screen (recall)
issues.sym: The backup camera picture is blank, frozen or does not appear when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: A fault in the camera or its software can leave no rear camera image. NHTSA recall 24V-951.
issues.next: Use the mirrors and turn your head when backing up. A Ford dealer will fix it under the recall.

issues.t: Electronic throttle body fault causes sudden power loss
issues.sym: The wrench light and check engine light come on, the engine suddenly loses most of its power or idles roughly, and it may stall. Turning the car off and back on can make it run normally again for a while.
issues.why: The electronic throttle body is the motor-driven valve that lets air into the engine. Dirt on its internal motor contacts or a bad connection makes it stick, so the computer limits power to protect the engine. Ford issued service bulletins for this on 2010-2011 and 2015-2016 Flex models.
issues.next: Get to a safe place, since power can drop at highway speed. Have a shop read the codes (often P2111, P2112 or P2119), check the wiring and connector, and replace the throttle body if needed. Ask a Ford dealer to check your VIN for any extended coverage.

issues.t: Cam timing codes and cold-start rattle from timing chain or phasers
issues.sym: A check engine light with cam timing codes such as P0016, a brief rattle like marbles in a can right after a cold start, rough idle, or sluggish power.
issues.why: The engine uses oil pressure to adjust cam timing through solenoids and cam phasers. Old or low oil can clog the solenoids, and over time the timing chain stretches or the phasers wear, so the cam and crank fall out of step.
issues.next: Check the oil level and change it if overdue, then have the codes read. A stuck solenoid is a small fix; a stretched chain is a big job, so ask the shop to replace the internal water pump at the same time since it sits behind the same cover.

issues.t: Radiator cooling fan stops working and engine overheats
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs when idling or in traffic, the A/C blows warm at stoplights, or the radiator fans never come on (or never shut off).
issues.why: The cooling fan module that runs the radiator fans is a common failure on early Flex models. Without the fans, the engine gets no airflow when the car isn't moving.
issues.next: If the gauge climbs, pull over and shut the engine off; driving an overheating engine can ruin it. Have a shop test the fans and fan control module before it leaves you stranded.
